title: Can spending one of the fourth junction’s outputs conceal which holders may join?
claim: After a three-parent fourth three-output junction spends exactly one output, decide whether the current unlabeled pair table fixes all legal three-parent choices. Test a live triple, holder changes and arbitrary reachable rivals, and distinguish the first spending move from later growth.
standard_statement: For a live reachable four-addition one-spent source, any isometry of minimum bond sizes clipped through six to any reachable mixed-law rival preserves every physical low star and the unique-holder status of the two remaining loose siblings. Possible full-site ambiguity reduces to two overlapping four-attachments of one high star. All one-spent sources through width 29 are uniquely realized. Several subfamilies have a complete all-size permission inverse.
prior_work: The unspent-output theorem of 001N resolves a rank-one extension from fresh coordinates. Its fixed 31-coordinate match becomes triple-negative immediately. An older fixed-name swap transports some suffixes. None of these results settles arbitrary histories after one output is spent.
completion_gate: Give an exact lawful one-spent history with a currently legal triple, or prove the specified population lacks one. Compare retained pair entries and marked verdicts under arbitrary relabeling. Settle a uniform case, an exact opposing witness or a precise residual after testing unrestricted rivals on identified examples.
source_contribution: Birth order and physical supports witness reachability and score true permissions. The reader receives only the current table, the formation law and the proposed unordered mark.

validation.status: V1 within-task symbolic proofs, independent proof audits and literal checks. Source-depth fixed point replayed under two hash seeds, named two-shrink example checked under permutation, connected cuts and independent parity-space minima agreed on all 465 entries of that width-31 example, arities 3–6 passed finite K1–K3. Separate referee pending.

conclusion: Once exactly one of the fourth junction’s outputs is spent, a live triple is possible and the same named triple can survive. At every finite size, distance five fixes both remaining loose outputs at a common holder and every other physical site of a live source. In the single-six case only four overlapping attachments of that site can vary. All 3,476 sources through width 29 have a unique physical completion. Whether an overlapping replacement can reverse a triple at larger widths is open.
evidence_class: All-size structural reductions and subfamily permission theorems with exact finite formation closure, literal witnesses and a bounded full inverse. General one-spent permission prediction open.
target_disposition: Existence, structural reduction, bounded complete inverse and all-size subfamily results proved. General one-spent triple invariance open.
unrestricted_obligation: For a live source beyond width 29, can distinct overlapping four-subsets attached to the sole six-place site, with the identical recovered smaller physical supports and surviving pair, give the same full named table and different menus? Both sides must be reachable. An opposition in which only an unrestricted rival is live need not satisfy the live-source reduction. The larger four-addition and unrestricted source families remain open.
failure_conditions: A positive source with three shrinking joins in the marked fixed point or a live two-six source with a shrink.
A through-five rival that spends a surviving sibling or changes a small physical support of a live source.
An all-rival alternative completion at width 29 or below, or a changed triple in a proved uniform branch.
